_note: Her Little Empire Income Fit Test opportunity database v1.1 (23 options). Field meanings in the header comment of options.py. Figures are labelled EST/FACT/UNKNOWN in text. AUD unless stated.

options.name: Specialist tutoring for adults and homeschool families (own clients)
options.do: Plan and teach 45-60 minute sessions online in a subject you know well: adult literacy, English for professionals, a language, exam prep for mature students, or homeschool families who need a specialist.
options.who_pays: Adults studying for work or migration, homeschooling parents, and parents of primary students (those sessions are after 3pm).
options.reach: A Superprof profile and school-gate or community word of mouth; referrals dominate after two clients.
options.first_test: Offer two free 30-minute sessions to people you know in your subject, in exchange for honest feedback and a quote request.
options.poor_fit: If you want only daytime hours, you depend on the adult and homeschool market, which is smaller; parents compare you with AU$25-31/hr platform tutors (EST, Australia).
options.verify: Private rates in your subject and area (UNKNOWN); whether daytime demand exists near you.

options.name: Language conversation lessons (Preply, italki, direct)
options.do: 45-60 minute video conversation lessons for adults overseas; their evenings fall in your school hours.
options.who_pays: Adult learners in Europe and the Americas; professionals preparing for relocation or exams.
options.reach: Platform marketplace: a 90-second profile video and your first ten reviews do the selling.
options.first_test: Create one profile with a video, set a trial price, and book three trial lessons this week.
options.poor_fit: Preply takes 33% of early lesson income; global price competition is intense; you must be at ease on camera.
options.verify: Typical rate for your language on the platform (UNKNOWN); your conversion from trial to regular.

options.name: Bookkeeping clean-up and software training (not regulated tax work)
options.do: Tidy receipt capture and coding, set up Xero, QuickBooks or MYOB properly, and train a sole trader to keep it that way, working under instruction from their accountant or registered agent.
options.who_pays: Sole traders and micro-businesses whose books are a mess before tax time; accountants who outsource the tidy-up.
options.reach: Local accountants and bookkeepers who need overflow help; local business groups; referrals.
options.first_test: Ask two local accountants or bookkeepers whether they outsource clean-up and training, and at what rate.
options.poor_fit: Tax work for a fee is regulated almost everywhere, and the line differs by country (Australia: BAS-agent registration for GST, BAS or payroll work; UK: anti-money-laundering supervision; US: a PTIN for paid tax preparation). Offshore competition is real.
options.verify: Local outsourcing rates (UNKNOWN); exactly where your country's regulator draws the line for each task you plan to offer.

options.name: Resume, LinkedIn and selection-criteria writing
options.do: Rewrite resumes and LinkedIn profiles; write public-sector selection criteria from a 30-minute intake call and the client's notes.
options.who_pays: Job-changers, public-sector applicants, mothers returning to work.
options.reach: Fiverr or a local jobs platform to start, LinkedIn, and word of mouth; public-sector applicants in your network.
options.first_test: Offer three free selection-criteria reviews in exchange for feedback and a quote request.
options.poor_fit: AI tools are eroding the budget tier; income is lumpy; revision scope creeps.
options.verify: Your conversion at AU$300-1,000 (EST, Australia) against AI-assisted competitors.

options.name: Social media management for local businesses
options.do: A monthly content calendar, 8-12 posts, scheduling and a simple report for two to four local businesses.
options.who_pays: Cafes, trades, clinics, boutiques whose pages have gone quiet.
options.reach: Pitching: send a one-post sample to three businesses with weak pages; referrals after the first two clients.
options.first_test: Make one sample post each for three local businesses and send it with a two-line offer.
options.poor_fit: It does not sell itself; scope creeps into evenings; owners cut it first when money is tight.
options.verify: Retainer level your local market bears (AU$1,500-5,000/mo is the broad agency-level AU range, EST).

options.name: Print-on-demand brand via Printify to Etsy
options.do: Design in Canva, list on Etsy, Printify prints and ships. You own the brand and the designs; no stock.
options.who_pays: Buyers in one narrow niche you understand (a hobby, a profession, a place).
options.reach: Etsy search and Pinterest; a niche with an identity beats a broad catalogue.
options.first_test: Draft six designs for one niche and test interest on a single Pinterest board before you list.
options.poor_fit: Heavily saturated; IP takedowns; 4-12 weeks to a first sale.
options.verify: Margin after Printify base cost and Etsy fees for your products (varies by item).

options.name: Personalised gifts and keepsakes (vinyl, laser, embroidery)
options.do: Make personalised keepsakes to order; production in school hours, post-office run at lunch.
options.who_pays: Gift buyers at Christmas, Mother's Day, births, weddings and school events.
options.reach: Etsy, local Facebook groups, school fetes and markets.
options.first_test: Make three samples and post them in two local community groups with a price.
options.poor_fit: Equipment capital; seasonality; licensed-character IP risk.
options.verify: Price band on Etsy for your product type; equipment cost for your chosen technique.

options.name: Alterations and repairs as a design-led service
options.do: Hems, zips, taking in, repairs and small remakes; drop-off and pickup in the day. Package it (a 'wardrobe refresh') rather than pricing by the hem.
options.who_pays: Local households, formal-season families, a dry cleaner's overflow.
options.reach: Local Facebook groups, local jobs platforms, a dry cleaner referral arrangement.
options.first_test: Post a 'hems and zips this week' offer in two local groups and tell your nearest dry cleaner you take overflow.
options.poor_fit: Per-item prices are low (median about AU$30, EST, Australia); packages are the only way to a decent hourly return.
options.verify: Local demand and price tolerance for packages.

options.name: Virtual assistant to online business manager
options.do: Inbox, calendar, invoicing, CRM and bookings in fixed weekly blocks; grow into managing launches and systems for two or three clients.
options.who_pays: Small-business owners who are past doing their own admin: consultants, allied-health practices, trades, online sellers.
options.reach: People you know first; Upwork and local jobs platforms; LinkedIn; referrals dominate from client two.
options.first_test: Message five small-business owners you know with a two-line 'five hours a week of inbox and calendar' offer.
options.poor_fit: Offshore price competition; clients wanting same-day replies outside your hours.
options.verify: Your rate against the AU freelance range (AU$35-65/hr, EST) and whether local clients will pay it.

options.name: Curated pre-loved fashion brand (Depop)
options.do: Photograph, list and post clothing; start with your own wardrobe, then curate a look from op shops and sell under a name.
options.who_pays: Younger buyers of a specific style; Depop charges sellers 0% in Australia since July 2026.
options.reach: The marketplace, plus an Instagram feed for the brand.
options.first_test: List 15 items from your own wardrobe this week and note which sell.
options.poor_fit: Low per-item value; returns disputes; curation takes taste and time.
options.verify: Which styles sell at what price for you.

options.name: Reselling via Facebook Marketplace and eBay
options.do: Source undervalued goods from op shops, clearances and kerbside; list, post or hand over locally in school hours.
options.who_pays: Local bargain hunters and collectors in categories you know.
options.reach: The marketplaces; eBay Australia charges nothing up to AU$25,000 in sales.
options.first_test: Spend AU$50 at two op shops or thrift stores, list ten items, and track what sells in 14 days.
options.poor_fit: Storage, slow stock, no-shows; it becomes a business to the ATO quickly.
options.verify: Your sourcing margin in practice.

options.name: Etsy digital downloads in a micro-niche
options.do: Design once in Canva and sell the file many times; viable only in a narrow niche you know better than the big shops.
options.who_pays: A specific group with a specific need (a profession, a hobby, a life event).
options.reach: Etsy search and Pinterest.
options.first_test: Search your niche on Etsy; if page one is all 1,000+ review shops, narrow again or drop it.
options.poor_fit: Saturation, piracy, algorithm dependence; 4-16 weeks to a first sale.
options.verify: Whether a page-one gap exists in your niche.

options.name: UGC video for brands
options.do: Film 15-60 second product videos at home for brands' ads. No following needed; pitching is.
options.who_pays: Small direct-to-consumer brands and the agencies that buy for them.
options.reach: UGC platforms (availability varies by country) and direct pitches to small local brands.
options.first_test: Film one 30-second sample for a product you own and send it to three small local brands.
options.poor_fit: Pitching-heavy, inconsistent, rights terms to negotiate.
options.verify: Platform availability in your country; per-video price you can command.

options.name: Affiliate content via Pinterest and a blog
options.do: Publish pins and posts in one narrow topic that link to retailer affiliate programs; an asset that compounds slowly.
options.who_pays: Readers planning a purchase in your topic; retailers pay the commission.
options.reach: Search and Pinterest traffic; no pitching.
options.first_test: Publish 20 pins to one board on one topic and measure clicks after 30 days before building a site.
options.poor_fit: Three to nine months to a first dollar; algorithm and AI-search dependence.
options.verify: Whether your topic gets clicks; commission rates by category.

options.name: Hosted room or granny flat on Airbnb
options.do: Host guests while you live on site; turnover cleans mid-morning. STRA registration, interconnected smoke alarms and strata rules apply.
options.who_pays: Travellers and short-stay workers in your area.
options.reach: The platform; price from three local listings.
options.first_test: Check your building (strata or HOA), city or council short-stay rules and your insurer, then list for one month.
options.poor_fit: Privacy; insurance and strata; seasonality; you need the space.
options.verify: Local nightly rates and occupancy; insurer's position.

options.name: Fractional HR and recruitment support
options.do: Onboarding packs, policy sets, job ads, interview guides, screening and reference checks, and a monthly people check-in for owner-operators with no HR person. Processes and documents, not legal advice.
options.who_pays: Owner-operators with 5-40 staff: trades, clinics, cafes, agencies.
options.reach: Referrals through bookkeepers and accountants, LinkedIn, local chambers; Expert360 for larger projects.
options.first_test: Offer one free 'hiring process review' to two businesses you know and ask what they would pay for the fixes.
options.poor_fit: Needs real HR experience and a warm network; clients want legal certainty you cannot give; award and dismissal questions must go to a lawyer or the Fair Work Ombudsman.
options.verify: Retainer level in your market (AU compilations cite AU$2,500-6,000/mo for 10-60 staff, EST).

options.name: Shopify store set-up and monthly care for local brands
options.do: Theme set-up, product uploads, shipping and payments configuration, launch checklist; then monthly store care. A free Shopify Partner account gives you practice stores.
options.who_pays: Local makers, boutiques, food producers and service businesses adding retail.
options.reach: Local referrals and markets, local jobs platforms, the Shopify Partner directory once eligible.
options.first_test: Build one practice store in a Partner dev account, then offer a fixed-price set-up to one local maker.
options.poor_fit: Marketplace price pressure from offshore (US$5-10/hr set-up bids exist); you need a local channel and a design or copy edge to charge AU$2,000+ (EST, Australia).
options.verify: Local demand; your package price between the Airtasker AU$200-400 tier and the AU$2,000+ agency tier (EST, Australia).

options.name: Pinterest management for product brands and bloggers
options.do: Keyword research, pin design, scheduling, board optimisation and a monthly report for brands in Pinterest-native niches.
options.who_pays: Etsy and Shopify sellers, bloggers, course creators, interiors and wedding brands.
options.reach: Creator communities, referrals from other VAs, direct outreach; mostly US-centred demand.
options.first_test: Offer one free 30-day Pinterest audit to a brand you follow and propose a starter retainer.
options.poor_fit: Offshore VA pricing at the bottom; results take months, so churn is real; little non-US rate evidence.
options.verify: Retainer level (US guides cite US$300-1,500/mo; no AU evidence).

options.name: Podcast and short-form video editing
options.do: Clean audio, cut, add intros and show notes in Descript; cut long videos into captioned vertical clips in CapCut; weekly batches.
options.who_pays: Small-business podcasters, coaches, local brands and creators.
options.reach: Upwork, local jobs platforms, podcast-host communities, referrals.
options.first_test: Edit one episode or three reels free for a creator you know and ask for a paid weekly batch.
options.poor_fit: Global price floor is low (US$20-40 per video bids exist); speed and taste are how you escape it; deadlines can be tight.
options.verify: Per-episode or per-batch price you can hold locally.

options.name: Canva template packs for one profession
options.do: Editable Canva bundles (social posts, price lists, client forms, brand kits) for a niche you know from the inside, sold as packs with custom brand kits as the upsell.
options.who_pays: Sole-trader professionals in that niche: celebrants, clinics, agents, trainers.
options.reach: Etsy search, Instagram and Pinterest, professional Facebook groups.
options.first_test: Make one five-template pack for your niche and offer it to ten people in that profession at a launch price.
options.poor_fit: Generic and real-estate templates are saturated; income is a long tail of small sales; the edge is niche knowledge, not design.
options.verify: Whether your niche buys on Etsy at all; Canva licence rules for templates.

options.name: Email flows and copy for small e-commerce brands
options.do: Write and build welcome, abandoned-cart and post-purchase flows in Klaviyo or Shopify Email; product descriptions; launch sequences; optional monthly campaigns.
options.who_pays: Direct-to-consumer brands doing AU$10K-100K a month; agencies white-labelling.
options.reach: Upwork Project Catalog, Shopify communities, LinkedIn, referrals from store set-up work.
options.first_test: Rewrite one brand's welcome flow free, measure clicks or revenue per recipient (open rates are unreliable), and quote the next two flows.
options.poor_fit: Crowded at the bottom (US$35 sequences); AI compresses prices; without a proof point you compete at the budget end (one established seller charges about US$400 a flow, EST).
options.verify: Per-flow price you can command once you have one result.

options.name: Translation and bilingual content (French, Spanish, English)
options.do: Translate and localise websites, product listings and marketing emails; bilingual captions and customer-service templates; subtitles. Commercial translation needs no certification; official documents need NAATI.
options.who_pays: Local exporters and tourism operators, e-commerce brands entering France, Spain or Latin America, agencies.
options.reach: ProZ, Upwork, direct approaches to exporters, agency vendor lists.
options.first_test: Translate one page of a local exporter's site as a sample and quote the rest at a per-word rate.
options.poor_fit: Machine translation has gutted low-end volume; agencies pay well under professional-association rates; value is in marketing localisation.
options.verify: Your per-word rate against your national translators' association guidance (AUSIT in Australia suggests AU$0.25/word) and agency reality.

options.name: Productised consulting from your former profession
options.do: Package what you used to do into a fixed-scope, fixed-price offer: a policy audit, a returning-to-work CV sprint, a grant-readiness review, a marketing check. Report plus action list in one to two weeks.
options.who_pays: Small businesses, not-for-profits and individuals who know your field needs doing and do not want to hire for it.
options.reach: LinkedIn and former colleagues first; Expert360 and Upwork Project Catalog later.
options.first_test: Write one package page with three tiers and send it to five former colleagues asking who needs it.
options.poor_fit: Needs a credible prior career and a warm network; some professions hit licensing walls (legal, financial advice, tax work).
options.verify: Package price for your field (resume tiers AU$300-1,000 are the one AU benchmark found, EST).
